B.narration:
You take out the bus ticket.

“4581”

That wasn't there when you put it in your pocket. The handwriting isn't yours.

The air grows thick, tasting of wet stone and stagnant dust.

Where you are: your apartment, 6C. With you: no one. The power is out; the only light is the storm's. Something impossible has just happened, and you have gone very still.
Write ONE short sentence (under 20 words) about what you sense in the room. No names, no numbers, no quotes, no words in ALL CAPS, and don't explain anything.

D.narration:
Then, from the stairwell, close and clear, a voice.

“I will meet you there soon.”

It's your voice. You haven't said a word.

The damp air presses against your skin, thick with the smell of wet earth and something metallic.

released_at: I will meet you there soon.

ending.text:
You open the door.

The other night comes in quietly, the way Mara did. It smells like rain that never reached this building.

Mara still has the key. In the other night she never let go of it, and she doesn't now.

Mara is in the stairwell. In the other night that is where she ended up, and that is where she is now. You don't go to her. She doesn't need you to anymore.

In 6D, Teo turns off his radio, and you hear him say, to no one, "Finally."

You look at what the night left you. "4581" on the bus ticket, in Mara's hand. And in the stairwell, your own voice, still saying "I will meet you there soon." to no one. Both from a night you never lived.

Both nights are true now. You will have to live in both of them.
